materialDissent: I do not fully accept the packet's Q3 framing that `unavailable: true` is merely vestigial. Observed in the diff: the index-lag branch returns `{ blocked: true, unavailable: true, reason: VERIFICATION_REASON.INDEX_LAG }` — but in that branch the search DID complete successfully (result.kind === 'matches', zero keys). The flag is not just unread, it is semantically false for the one case this round is carving out. Inference: if any future consumer or audit-shaping code reads it, it will reclassify a completed-search index-lag block as a search availability failure, which is the exact conflation exit 20 exists to remove. This is non-blocking for me (grep evidence in the packet shows zero readers today, and it predates this diff), but I dissent from calling it purely cosmetic and recommend it be dropped from the index-lag branch, or renamed, in a follow-up rather than left indefinitely.
review.recommendation: Approve as-is; do not open another round on this diff. The round-7 evidence closes my round-6 objection: the consumer search is now genuinely unfiltered (`grep -rl \"kstack-jira\" . --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=node_modules`, no `--include`), and the enumerated result set — package.json passthrough, the two test files, six SKILL.md files restricted to `draft`/`doctor`, CONFIG.md, and .kstack prose — contains no numeric-exit-status branching. Within this repository there is no in-repo consumer that exit 2→20 can break. Q1's pasted paragraph now enumerates all four exit-2 cases and matches JIRA_QUEUE.md's wording; Q2 confirms the interface change was an explicit owner decision and that JIRA_QUEUE.md plus the CLI help text are the only exit-code-enumerating surfaces this project has, both already updated. Code correctness re-checked independently this round: `gateExitCode()` reads only `keys` and `reason`, the only producer of `reason: 'index-lag'` is the measurable-sub-floor branch, and `youngestMarkerAgeMs()` returning `null` instead of `0` for unmeasurable ages is behavior-preserving at every call site (both `0` and `null` already failed `>= minimumMarkerAgeMs`), so the change is label-accuracy plus one new explicit unmeasurable branch in the gate — no widening of what blocks. Exit 20 does not collide with shell-reserved codes (126/127/128+) and is added to the collision-inventory assertion. Follow-up items, all optional and none gating: (1) drop or rename `unavailable: true` on the index-lag return so the flag stops contradicting the case it accompanies; (2) consider one assertion that submit's retry-verification-interval wait still exits 2 — it is hardcoded `EXIT.STATE_ERROR` so it cannot regress silently today, but it is the one exit-2 case named in the docs with no test binding it; (3) runVerification's `marker-younger-than-index-lag-minimum` label is unasserted, though it is the unchanged pre-existing literal, so it carries no new risk.
review.strongestObjection: The strongest remaining objection is the one in materialDissent: the index-lag branch still returns `unavailable: true` alongside `reason: 'index-lag'`, even though that branch is reached only after a successfully completed zero-match search. It is a false field on the newly-distinguished path, kept out of scope for a label-accuracy round whose entire purpose was label accuracy. It cannot cause a defect today (grep shows no readers, and `gateExitCode()` never consults it), so it does not block, but leaving it is a small latent trap for exactly the distinction this addition creates. A secondary, weaker point: because this ships as a plugin, out-of-repository callers matching on exit 2 are unverifiable from inside this repo — the packet is right that no changelog mechanism exists to notify them, so the mitigation is the owner's accepted risk, not a technical control.
